The list names research JOBS rather than the word research, for the same reason the leadership row does: `professor of research methods` names a subject, not a second post, and is deliberately not matched. Lifted from the 1.17 vocabulary so it is multilingual from the first line - investigador, chercheur, ricercatore, pesquisador, Forscher, wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter, arastirmaci.

The mirror on the research side, and the largest single effect of this change. `research professor` 48,609 records and `research assistant professor` 71,785 are research posts that also teach, and Lecturer has never contained them - which is why the survey check scored Lecturer against people whose own answer was `professor`. Measured in analyses/50 before it landed.

MERVE 2026-11-11, question 6.1b. `doctoral researcher` 42,231 records and `postgraduate researcher` 5,427 are doctoral students who describe themselves in research terms, so 1.17's loose reading keeps them in Researcher - and the Students audience then does not contain them. This row puts them in both. THE VETO IS THE WHOLE RISK HERE. `postdoctoral researcher` contains `doctoral` only across a word boundary RE2 does not see, so post-doc forms are vetoed explicitly in six spellings; and the senior words are vetoed because 24 of the 25 largest titles in the senior half of this group carry `phd` as a CREDENTIAL rather than a status, which is the finding that scoped 1.17 to the early end.
